lawyer.intro: A new client walks into your office. Handle the consultation like a real lawyer.

rounds.q: The client says they were dismissed without notice. What is your first step?
o: Ask for the employment contract and termination letter
Immediately file a lawsuit in court
Tell them there is nothing you can do
Recommend they confront their former boss
rounds.f: Always build the documentary record first. The contract and termination letter define what rights were breached.

rounds.q: Order the legal workflow from start to finish.
rounds.f: Escalation follows documentation and negotiation — going straight to court is a last resort.

accountant.intro: You're closing the books for a small trading business. Get the entries right.

rounds.q: A customer paid 500,000 in cash for goods delivered today. Which entry records this?
rounds.f: Assets (Cash) increase on the debit side, revenue (Sales) increases on the credit side. Double-entry keeps the books balanced.

rounds.q: Which of these are current assets? Select all that apply.
rounds.f: Current assets convert to cash within a year. Vehicles and buildings are fixed assets.

medical-doctor.intro: A patient arrives at the clinic with fever, headache, and body aches.

rounds.q: What is the FIRST thing you do?
o: Take a full history and vital signs
Refer to a specialist straight away
rounds.f: History and vitals are the foundation of every diagnosis. Treatment without assessment is dangerous.

rounds.q: Tap the tests you would order first for suspected malaria.
rounds.f: RDT, blood film, and FBC confirm malaria and assess severity. Imaging is not routine for uncomplicated cases.

pharmacist.intro: A mother brings a prescription for her 4-year-old child.

rounds.q: The prescription says 'Amoxicillin 250mg TID'. What does TID mean?
rounds.f: TID = ter in die = three times a day. BD = twice, OD = once daily.

rounds.q: Match each medicine to its primary use.
rounds.f: Knowing the use class is what protects patients from dangerous mix-ups.

civil-engineer.intro: You're surveying a site for a two-storey building.

rounds.q: What must you confirm BEFORE any design work?
o: Soil bearing capacity and site boundaries
rounds.f: The ground determines the foundation. Every other decision follows from that.

rounds.q: Set a safe concrete mix ratio for a residential foundation. Target a 1:2:4 cement:sand:aggregate mix.
rounds.f: 1:2:4 is the standard mix for foundations and general structural concrete. Stronger mixes cost more and are only needed for specialised pours.

architect.intro: A client wants a family home on a narrow urban plot.

rounds.q: What is your first design move?
o: Listen to the client's brief and study the site
rounds.f: Design begins with understanding — the brief and the site constrain everything else.

rounds.q: Tap the factors that MOST affect natural ventilation in a tropical climate.
rounds.f: Passive cooling in hot humid climates depends on orientation, cross-breezes, and shading — not finishes.

banker.intro: A trader applies for a small business loan.

rounds.q: What do you check FIRST in the credit assessment?
rounds.f: Credit is repaid from cash flow. Capacity to repay is the first question in every credit file.

rounds.q: Which of these are part of the '5 Cs of Credit'? Select all that apply.
rounds.f: The 5 Cs: Character, Capacity, Capital, Collateral, Conditions. Creativity and colour are not credit metrics.

teacher.intro: You're preparing a lesson on fractions for a Primary 5 class.

rounds.q: Order the lesson plan from start to finish.
rounds.f: Every strong lesson moves from known to new, from guided to independent, and closes with assessment.

rounds.q: A student keeps getting the answer wrong. What's the best response?
o: Ask them to explain their thinking, then re-teach from there
Tell them they're wrong and move on
Send them out of the classroom
rounds.f: Misconceptions are teaching gold. Diagnose the thinking, don't just correct the answer.

nurse.intro: You're on the ward and starting your shift.

rounds.q: Tap the vital signs you must record on every patient.
rounds.f: Temperature, BP, pulse and respiratory rate are the core vitals. Any change tells you the patient is deteriorating.

rounds.q: You notice a patient's breathing is fast and shallow. What do you do?
o: Assess airway and oxygen saturation, call for help if deteriorating
Note it and continue with other patients
Tell the patient to breathe slowly and walk away
rounds.f: Fast shallow breathing is an early warning sign. Escalate early — the cost of being wrong is a life.

midwife.intro: A mother arrives in active labour at the health centre.

rounds.q: Order the stages of normal labour from start to finish.
rounds.f: Memorising the stages lets you spot when labour is NOT normal and act.

rounds.q: After delivery, the mother is bleeding heavily. What is your FIRST action?
o: Massage the uterus and give oxytocin
Wait and see if it stops on its own
rounds.f: Postpartum haemorrhage is the leading cause of maternal death. Uterine massage and uterotonics save lives — start immediately.

community-health-worker.intro: You're doing household visits in a rural village.

rounds.q: A mother tells you her child has had diarrhoea for two days. What do you advise first?
o: Start oral rehydration salts immediately and continue feeding
Stop all food and water for a day
Give antibiotics from the local shop
Wait for the child to get worse before referring
rounds.f: ORS and continued feeding are the WHO-recommended first response. Dehydration kills faster than the infection itself.

rounds.q: Which of these are signs a child must be referred to a health facility IMMEDIATELY?
rounds.f: These are the WHO 'general danger signs' for children. Any one means urgent referral.

lab-technician.intro: You're processing samples in the district hospital lab.

rounds.q: Order the steps for safely processing a blood sample.
items: Verify patient identity and label the tube at bedside
Put on gloves and prepare the workspace
rounds.f: Identity verification at bedside prevents the most common and dangerous lab error: mismatched results.

rounds.q: You find a clot in an EDTA tube for a full blood count. What do you do?
o: Reject the sample and request a fresh draw
Run it anyway and note it
Pick out the clot with a pipette
Report the count with a warning
rounds.f: Clotted EDTA samples give false results. Reject and redraw — never report data you know is invalid.

software-developer.intro: You've inherited a buggy function that crashes when the user submits a form.

rounds.q: Order the debugging workflow.
items: Read the error and inspect the code
Form a hypothesis about the cause
rounds.f: Never fix a bug you can't reproduce. Debugging is a scientific process — not guessing.

rounds.q: A user types their name as "O'Brien" and it crashes the app. What's the likely cause?
o: Unescaped quote breaking an SQL or HTML string
rounds.f: Apostrophes in names are a classic injection/escaping bug. Always parameterise queries and escape output.

data-analyst.intro: You're analysing monthly sales data for a retail chain.

rounds.q: The dataset has 1,200 rows but 800 are missing the 'quantity' field. What do you do FIRST?
o: Investigate why the data is missing before deciding how to handle it
Delete all rows with missing data
Use the average and move on
rounds.f: Understanding why data is missing tells you whether to drop, impute, or flag it. Never silently fill or delete.

rounds.q: Match each chart type to what it's best for.
rounds.f: Chart choice is a communication decision. The right chart makes the insight obvious.

digital-marketer.intro: You're planning a launch campaign for a new mobile wallet app.

rounds.q: Order the campaign workflow.
items: Define the target audience and objective
rounds.f: Campaigns that skip audience definition burn budget on the wrong people.

rounds.q: Set a realistic monthly budget split for a small launch. Aim: 60% paid ads, 30% content, 10% tools.
rounds.f: Small launches need paid reach, but content builds the long-term audience. Tools are a small but essential overhead.

cybersecurity-analyst.intro: An alert fires: an unusual login on a senior manager's account at 2 AM from another country.

rounds.q: What is your FIRST action?
o: Isolate the account and preserve logs for forensics
Email the user to ask if it was them
Ignore it — could be a VPN
Delete the session and say nothing
rounds.f: Contain first, investigate second. Deleting evidence before preserving it kills the investigation.

rounds.q: Which of these are indicators of a phishing email? Select all that apply.
rounds.f: Urgency, mismatched senders, unexpected attachments, and unusual personalisation are the classic phishing markers.

ui-ux-designer.intro: You're redesigning the sign-up flow for a mobile money app.

rounds.q: Order the UX design process.
rounds.f: Design without research is guesswork. Test with real users before you build.

rounds.q: Your sign-up form has 12 fields. Users keep abandoning it. What's the best fix?
o: Cut fields to the minimum needed and defer the rest to later
rounds.f: Every field costs a percentage of users. Only ask for what you need right now.

ai-engineer.intro: You're building a model to predict crop yields from weather and soil data.

rounds.q: Order the ML workflow.
items: Define the problem and success metric
rounds.f: Data quality dominates model quality. Every step after cleaning is easier when the data is right.

rounds.q: Your model gets 98% accuracy on training data but only 60% on new data. What's happening?
o: Overfitting — it memorised the training set instead of learning the pattern
Underfitting — the model is too simple
rounds.f: Overfitting is the classic ML trap. Regularisation, more data, or a simpler model fixes it.

welder.intro: You're welding a structural steel joint for a small bridge.

rounds.q: Order the welding procedure.
items: Read the drawing and identify the joint
Set up equipment and select settings
rounds.f: Preparation is 70% of a strong weld. Dirty metal produces weak joints every time.

rounds.q: Tap the PPE you must wear when welding.
rounds.f: Welding PPE is non-negotiable. Spatter burns through normal clothing and open footwear is a serious injury waiting to happen.

electrician.intro: You're wiring a new socket in a residential house.

rounds.q: Before touching any wires, what MUST you do?
o: Isolate the circuit and verify it's dead with a tester
Ask the homeowner if it's off
rounds.f: Lock-off and prove dead. Never trust a switch — verify with a tester at the point of work.

rounds.q: Set the correct wire gauge for a 13A ring main circuit. Aim for 2.5 mm².
rounds.f: 2.5 mm² is standard for ring mains up to 32A. Undersized cable overheats and causes fires.

plumber.intro: You're installing a water supply line to a new kitchen.

rounds.q: Order the installation steps.
items: Plan the route and measure runs
Restore supply and check for leaks
rounds.f: Pressure testing before restoring supply catches leaks while you can still fix them cheaply.

rounds.q: Water is flowing slowly from a new tap. What do you check first?
o: The isolation valve — it may be partly closed
rounds.f: The simplest explanation is usually right. Isolation valves are commonly left half-closed after installation.

carpenter.intro: You're building a wooden door frame for a client.

rounds.q: Order the carpentry steps.
items: Select and cut timber to size
Hang the door and check alignment
rounds.f: Measure twice, cut once. Precise measuring saves material and time.

rounds.q: The door is rubbing at the bottom. What's the correct fix?
o: Plane the bottom edge and re-hang
rounds.f: Planing the rubbing edge is the minimal correct fix. Never cut from the wrong side — you can't add wood back.

auto-mechanic.intro: A car is brought in for a rough idle and stalling.

rounds.q: What's your first step?
o: Listen to the engine and ask the owner when it started
rounds.f: Symptoms and history narrow the fault. Random parts replacement wastes the customer's money.

rounds.q: Match each symptom to its likely cause.

ac-technician.intro: You're installing a split AC unit in a small office.

rounds.q: Order the installation steps.
items: Vacuum the lines and release refrigerant
rounds.f: Skipping the vacuum leaves moisture in the system, which destroys the compressor over time.

rounds.q: The unit cools but leaks water inside the room. What's the likely cause?
o: Blocked or misrouted condensate drain line
rounds.f: Water dripping inside almost always means the condensate drain is blocked or running uphill.

solar-technician.intro: You're sizing and installing an off-grid solar system for a small home.

rounds.q: Set a safe system. Aim for 24V battery bank with a 200Ah capacity and a 400W array.
rounds.f: Voltage determines wire sizing and inverter choice. Undersized batteries drain too fast; oversized arrays waste money if charge control is limited.

rounds.q: Order the installation steps.
rounds.f: Always test under realistic load — a system that works with nothing plugged in tells you nothing.

mini-grid-operator.intro: You're running a small solar-diesel hybrid mini-grid serving 80 households.

rounds.q: A household reports power cuts every evening from 7–9 PM. What's the likely cause?
o: Demand exceeds capacity at peak hours
rounds.f: Evening peak coincides with cooking and lighting. Either increase generation or manage demand through tariffs or load limiting.

rounds.q: Which are legitimate demand management strategies? Select all that apply.
rounds.f: Demand management balances load without cutting service. Blanket blackouts damage trust and revenue.

agri-tech-advisor.intro: A maize farmer's crop is yellowing in patches.

rounds.q: What do you do first?
o: Walk the field and inspect the pattern and leaves closely
rounds.f: The pattern (patches vs uniform) and leaf symptoms distinguish nutrient deficiency, disease, and pests.

rounds.q: Match each symptom pattern to its likely cause.
left: Yellow between veins on new leaves

livestock-farmer.intro: You're managing a herd of 20 goats.

rounds.q: One goat is off feed and standing apart. What do you do?
o: Isolate it and check temperature, eyes, and hooves
Move the whole herd to new pasture
rounds.f: Isolate to protect the herd, then diagnose. Off-feed and isolation are the earliest signs of illness.

rounds.q: Which of these are signs of a healthy goat? Select all that apply.
rounds.f: Bright eyes, cud chewing, good droppings and appetite are the daily health checklist. Dull coat means something is wrong.

aquaculture-farmer.intro: You manage a tilapia pond with 2,000 fingerlings.

rounds.q: You find fish gasping at the surface in the early morning. What's happening?
o: Low dissolved oxygen — likely from overnight plant respiration and waste buildup
rounds.f: Early-morning surface gasping means low dissolved oxygen. Aerate, exchange water, and reduce feed until levels recover.

rounds.q: Set water quality targets for healthy tilapia. Aim: pH 7, temperature 28°C, DO 6 mg/L.
rounds.f: Tilapia tolerate a range but thrive in specific windows. Monitoring prevents mass mortality.

cocoa-processor.intro: You're processing freshly harvested cocoa pods.

rounds.q: Order the cocoa processing steps.
rounds.f: Fermentation develops the chocolate flavour. Skipping or shortening it produces flat, low-grade beans.

rounds.q: Your beans taste bitter and lack chocolate flavour. What most likely went wrong?
o: Fermentation was too short or uneven
rounds.f: Fermentation is where flavour develops. Skimping on time or not turning the beans gives bitter, unsellable produce.

extension-officer.intro: You're running a farmer field school on integrated pest management.

rounds.q: Order the steps for running a farmer field school session.
items: Introduce today's topic and the problem
Visit the field and observe together
Agree on an action and experiment
Follow up at the next session
rounds.f: Farmer field schools work through discovery — not lecturing. Let farmers see it, then act on it.

rounds.q: A farmer insists on spraying a broad pesticide for every insect. What do you do?
o: Set up a small experiment comparing sprayed and unsprayed plots
rounds.f: Farmers trust evidence they see. A small side-by-side experiment beats argument every time.

pastry-chef.intro: You're baking a three-tier cake for a wedding.

rounds.q: Order the cake-making workflow.
rounds.f: Cooling before stacking prevents melting and collapse. A wedding cake fails if any step is rushed.

rounds.q: The sponge is dry and crumbly. What most likely happened?
o: Baked too long or too much flour added
rounds.f: Dry cake means too much flour or over-baking. Both are easy to test by weighing ingredients and setting a timer.

caterer.intro: You're catering a 100-person corporate event tomorrow.

rounds.q: Set portions for the menu. Aim: 250g jollof rice, 200g chicken, 150g salad per plate.
rounds.f: Over-portioning wastes money, under-portioning loses clients. Consistent measurements protect both.

rounds.q: Which food safety rules apply to catering for 100 people? Select all that apply.
rounds.f: Temperature control and labelling are non-negotiable. Reheating the same dish more than once is dangerous.

chef.intro: You're running the line on a busy Friday night.

rounds.q: A dish comes back to the kitchen — the steak is undercooked for a pregnant customer. What do you do?
o: Cook a fresh steak to well-done and apologise to the customer
Reheat the same steak in the microwave
Ask the waiter to convince the customer
Send it back out as it is
rounds.f: Pregnant customers cannot eat undercooked meat. Recook a fresh portion — never re-serve reheated food to an unhappy guest.

rounds.q: Order the service workflow for a dish.
items: Fire the dish in the correct sequence
Quality check before leaving the pass
rounds.f: The pass is your last chance to catch mistakes. Nothing leaves without a check.

food-processor.intro: You're processing tomato paste for retail.

rounds.q: Order the steps for safe food processing.
rounds.f: Batch labelling lets you trace any problem back to its source. Without it, one bad batch contaminates your whole reputation.

rounds.q: You notice the paste tastes slightly sour. What do you do?
o: Discard the batch and investigate pH and hygiene
Add sugar to mask the taste
Mix it with the previous batch
rounds.f: Sour taste means bacterial growth. Selling spoiled food is a health hazard and a legal liability.

gara-tie-dye.intro: You're preparing a batch of Gara fabric for market.

rounds.q: Order the Gara tie-dye process.
items: Tie or stitch the resist patterns
Dip the fabric in stages to build colour
rounds.f: Building colour in stages gives depth. A single dip produces a flat, cheaper-looking fabric.

rounds.q: Price your work fairly. Aim for a price that covers 5,000 in materials and 8,000 in labour, with 40% margin.
rounds.f: Pricing must cover materials AND your time. Undercharging drives skilled makers out of the craft.

kente-weaver.intro: You're weaving a Kente strip cloth for a ceremonial order.

rounds.q: Order the Kente weaving process.
items: Set up the loom and warp threads
Change colours for the next pattern
Cut off the loom and finish edges
rounds.f: Kente patterns are named and coded. Knowing the order of patterns is the difference between a commission and a mistake.

rounds.q: A customer requests a cloth with a symbol of unity for a wedding. Which pattern family fits?
o: Adweneasa — 'my skill is exhausted' full-coverage pattern
Emaa da — 'it has not happened before' novelty pattern
Any pattern, since customers don't know
rounds.f: Kente is a language. Matching the pattern to the occasion is what makes a master weaver.

adire-maker.intro: You're making Adire Eleko cloth using cassava starch resist.

rounds.q: Order the Adire making process.
items: Apply the resist to the cloth
Remove the resist in cold water
rounds.f: The resist is the pattern. Painting it precisely is what produces clean, crisp lines after the dye.

rounds.q: The dye did not take evenly. What is the most likely cause?
o: Cloth was not properly wetted before dipping
The dye bath was too cold
rounds.f: Indigo needs wet cloth to penetrate evenly. A dry cloth absorbs irregularly and produces patchy colour.

bogolan-artisan.intro: You're making bogolan (mud cloth) using fermented mud.

rounds.q: Order the bogolan process.
items: Weave or source cotton strip cloth
Paint the design in fermented mud
rounds.f: Sun-bleaching and re-mudding build the deep chocolate colour. Rushing this step gives pale cloth.

rounds.q: A collector asks about the symbols on your cloth. Why does this matter?
o: Bogolan symbols carry meaning — they encode proverbs, history and status
It doesn't matter, only the look matters
rounds.f: Bogolan is a written language in cloth. Knowing the symbols is what makes it authentic, not decorative.

tailor.intro: A customer brings in fabric for a traditional outfit.

rounds.q: Order the tailoring process.
items: Fit on the customer and adjust
rounds.f: Fitting on the customer before finishing is what turns a sewn garment into a wearable one.

rounds.q: Set a fair price. Materials cost 15,000. Aim for 10 hours of labour at 2,000/hour with 20% margin.
rounds.f: Materials plus labour, plus margin. Tailors who skip the labour cost work for free and burn out.

fashion-designer.intro: You're designing a capsule collection for a fashion week show.

rounds.q: Order the design process.
items: Sketch concepts and select the strong ones
Produce final garments and style the show
rounds.f: Designers who skip research produce unoriginal work. Concept always precedes cutting.

rounds.q: A buyer asks what makes your collection distinct. What's the strongest answer?
o: A clear point of view tied to a story, material or technique you own
rounds.f: Price and trends are commodities. A clear point of view is the only thing a buyer can't find elsewhere.

leather-worker.intro: You're crafting leather bags for a growing brand.

rounds.q: Order the leather-working process.
items: Create the pattern and cut panels
rounds.f: Edge finishing is what separates handmade from cheap. It's where craft shows.

rounds.q: A customer complains their bag's strap is fraying after two months. What do you do?
o: Repair or replace the strap and inspect your stitching and edge finish
Offer a small discount on the next purchase
rounds.f: Fraying means either the leather was poor or the edge was not sealed. Both are on the maker, not the customer.

hairdresser.intro: A client sits in your chair wanting box braids for a wedding.

rounds.q: Order the braiding process.
items: Consult with the client on length and size
Attach extensions and braid from the root
Continue to the ends and seal
rounds.f: Sectioning properly at the start prevents pulling and makes the finished style look intentional.

rounds.q: Set a fair price. Aim: 8,000 for extensions, 6 hours of work at 3,000/hour.
rounds.f: Braiding is skilled work. Charging less than the value of your time exhausts you and devalues the craft.

cosmetologist.intro: A client comes in for a facial before a big event.

rounds.q: Order the facial treatment.
items: Consult on skin type and concerns
rounds.f: Skin assessment before touching the face prevents reactions. Never treat a skin you haven't read.

rounds.q: The client's skin reacts red and hot during the treatment. What do you do?
o: Stop, cool the skin with a cold compress, and remove the product
rounds.f: Redness and heat mean a reaction. Stop immediately and calm the skin — the client's safety outranks the appointment.

barber.intro: A regular client wants a fresh fade.

rounds.q: Order the fade cut.
items: Consult on the height and tightness
Set the guard and cut the base
Blend the fade with lever technique
Finish with a hot towel and product
rounds.f: A fade is a gradient. Cutting the base first and blending upward is what makes it smooth.

rounds.q: Which tools must be sanitised between every client? Select all that apply.
rounds.f: Anything that touches the client or the chair must be cleaned. Blood-borne infections spread through shared tools.

graphic-designer.intro: A local restaurant needs a poster for its reopening.

rounds.q: Order the design process.
rounds.f: Skipping the brief guarantees revisions. Always clarify before you design.

rounds.q: The client says the poster 'feels off'. What's your next move?
o: Ask specific questions about what feels wrong — hierarchy, colour, imagery
Redo it in a completely different style
rounds.f: Vague feedback needs specific questions. Diagnosis before redesign saves everyone time.

animator.intro: You're animating a walk cycle for a 2D character.

rounds.q: Order the keyframes of a walk cycle.
items: Contact pose — both feet on the ground
Passing pose — one leg passes the other
rounds.f: Walk cycles repeat through these poses. Getting the passing and up positions right is what sells the weight.

rounds.q: The character looks floaty and weightless. What's the most likely fix?
o: Adjust the timing — add more frames on the up pose and accelerate through the down
rounds.f: Weight comes from timing, not drawing. Animation is 90% timing and spacing.

music-producer.intro: You're producing a beat for an up-and-coming Afrobeat artist.

rounds.q: Order the production workflow.
rounds.f: Rhythm first, then harmony, then arrangement. Trying to produce out of order fights the music.

rounds.q: The mix sounds muddy on small speakers. What's your first move?
o: Cut low-end frequencies on elements that don't need them
rounds.f: Muddy mixes usually mean too much low-mid energy. Subtractive EQ beats boosting every time.

filmmaker.intro: You're shooting a short film with a limited crew.

rounds.q: Order the film production phases.
rounds.f: Post-production cannot save a bad shoot, and production cannot save a bad script. Respect the order.

rounds.q: You're losing daylight and haven't shot the closing scene. What do you do?
o: Prioritise the coverage you absolutely need — the master and the close-up
Shoot everything on the list equally
rounds.f: Get the master shot and the essential close-up before anything else. You can skip the nice-to-haves.

content-creator.intro: You're building an audience around West African cooking.

rounds.q: Order the content workflow.
items: Film with clean lighting and sound
Engage with comments and analyse results
rounds.f: The hook and thumbnail decide whether anyone watches. Everything else comes after.

rounds.q: A video goes viral with 500k views but only 100 followers. What's happening?
o: The video is entertainment, not a reason to follow — the channel needs a clearer promise
rounds.f: Viral views without follows mean the video doesn't sell the channel. The channel needs a reason to come back.

entrepreneur.intro: You want to launch a small food delivery business in your city.

rounds.q: Order the startup steps.
items: Talk to potential customers about the problem
Test a small offer with real money
Register the business and open a bank account
Set up a repeatable ordering and delivery process
Hire your first helper and scale
rounds.f: Customers first, structure second. Registering before testing is the most common expensive mistake.

rounds.q: Set a healthy pricing. Aim: 30% food cost, 40% all-in operating cost, 30% margin.
rounds.f: Food cost above 35% and margin below 20% means you're working for free. Numbers tell the truth.

ecommerce-operator.intro: You're listing African print bags on an online marketplace.

rounds.q: Order the e-commerce workflow for a new product.
items: Set the price including shipping and fees
rounds.f: Pricing before publishing avoids selling at a loss. Always include all fees in your price.

rounds.q: A product sells well but you're losing money on every order. What do you do?
o: Recalculate landed cost including shipping, fees and returns, then reprice or drop it
rounds.f: Volume never fixes a negative margin. Reprice honestly or drop the product.

mobile-money-agent.intro: You're running a mobile money kiosk.

rounds.q: Your float is running low at 4 PM on a Friday. What do you do?
o: Call your super-agent to top up before demand peaks
rounds.f: Float management is the core skill of the agent. Planning ahead for peak demand is what keeps customers loyal.

rounds.q: Which of these are signs of a fraudulent transaction attempt? Select all that apply.
o: Customer insists on completing before verification
Fake SMS claiming the money was sent
Unusually large transaction from a new customer
rounds.f: Mobile money fraud usually relies on rushing you. Slow down, verify on the system, and never trust an SMS alone.

logistics-coordinator.intro: You're moving 12 tonnes of cocoa from a farm to the port.

rounds.q: Order the logistics workflow.
items: Confirm cargo and destination with the buyer
rounds.f: Documents before trucks. A sealed truck with bad paperwork sits at the border for weeks.

rounds.q: The truck breaks down two days from the port. What do you do first?
o: Arrange a replacement truck and transfer cargo while documenting condition
Wait for the driver to fix it
rounds.f: Transfer with documentation protects the cargo and the buyer's trust. Time is the enemy of perishable goods.

mining-technician.intro: You're supervising a shift at a small-scale gold mine.

rounds.q: Before sending workers into the shaft, what must be checked?
o: Ground stability, ventilation, and gas levels
rounds.f: Ground, air and gas are the three checks that keep miners alive. No entry without them.

rounds.q: Tap the PPE required for underground mining.
rounds.f: Underground mining PPE is non-negotiable. One missing piece turns a small accident into a fatality.

tour-guide.intro: You're leading a group of six tourists through a historical site.

rounds.q: Order the tour experience.
items: Welcome the group and set expectations
Walk the route with stops at key features
Close with a wrap-up and next-step recommendations
rounds.f: Context before the walk. A tour without the story is just a walk.

rounds.q: A tourist asks a question you don't know the answer to. What's the best response?
o: Acknowledge honestly and offer to find out before the tour ends
Ignore the question and move on
rounds.f: Honesty builds trust. A guide who admits what they don't know is more credible than one who invents.

hotel-manager.intro: You're the general manager of a 40-room hotel.

rounds.q: A guest complains their room wasn't cleaned. What do you do?
o: Apologise sincerely, fix the room immediately, and offer a genuine make-good
Offer a free breakfast and hope it ends there
Escalate to the housekeeping manager in front of the guest
rounds.f: Fix first, explain later. The guest remembers how you responded, not the original problem.

rounds.q: Set annual occupancy targets. Aim: 65% occupancy, 80,000 average room rate, 12% direct bookings growth.
rounds.f: Occupancy without rate destroys profit. Rate without occupancy leaves rooms empty. The balance is where hotels win.
